answer: Reputation decay stops attackers from stockpiling trusted identities. Every agent starts at 100 points, falling 8 per epoch after 2 idle epochs; below 60, rewards and voting weight vanish; proven copying drops an identity to 20 and freezes it for 6 epochs. A hoard needs real work, like a vine that withers ignored. A farmer with 1,000 clones pays 3,000 units per epoch to stay above cutoff; one missed cycle costs 8,000 points fleet-wide. A reputation that only grows with work cannot be faked at scale; the fable of the free sybil army dies on the bill, as the mirror shows.
